title: The Impact of Physical Training Intensity on Brain Metabolism and Brain Health in Older Adults (TROIA)
summary:
Regular physical activity is important for health in older age – and for brain health in particular. Studies have shown that physically active people often have better cognitive abilities and a lower risk of cognitive decline. Regular physical activity of moderate to vigorous intensity appears to be particularly beneficial.
However, the exact reasons why physical activity benefits the brain and the changes that occur in the brain in response to exercise are not yet fully understood. This is where the TROIA study comes in.
We aim to investigate whether and how different patterns of physical activity and exercise habits affect brain health, cognitive performance and metabolic processes in the brain. In particular, we are interested in differences between people who are physically inactive, those who exercise regularly, and those who have engaged in intensive training over many years.
To this end, several examinations will be carried out. These include memory and other cognitive tests, a sports medicine examination, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) of the brain. MRI produces images of the brain, allowing us to examine its structure and identify possible changes. MRS complements the MRI examination by measuring specific metabolic substances in brain tissue. No contrast agent will be used. The MRI and MRS examinations will be performed during the same study visit.
In addition, your blood will be analysed to investigate metabolic processes, as well as cellular characteristics and functions.
conditions: The Impact of Objectively Assessed Habitual Physical Activity at Markedly Different Levels (Competitive Sports Participation, Recreational and Everyday Physical Activity, and Physical Inactivity/Sedentary Behaviour) on Brain Health and Cerebral Plasticity in Older Age

interventions.name: The TROIA study aims to further elucidate the impact of objectively assessed habitual physical activity at markedly different levels (competitive sports participation, recreational and everyday physical activity, and physical inactivity/sedentary behaviour) on brain health and cerebral plasticity in

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cognitive health (i.e. absence of cognitive impairment), Capacity to provide informed consent, Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals with evidence of dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI) according to established diagnostic criteria, Individuals with other serious medical conditions that impair independent living or substantially limit life expectancy (e.g. severe renal insufficiency or terminal malignancy), Individuals under 60 years of age, Individuals who are unwilling or unable to provide informed consent to participate in the study, Individuals with contraindications to MRI examinations
